name: Switchr — Indian Festivals & Holidays
note: Bundled offline data: major Indian festivals, gazetted (national) holidays and observances. Types: national = gazetted/public holiday, festival = major religious/cultural festival, observance = minor observance.
source: Dates cross-checked against timeanddate.com/holidays/india and drikpanchang.com. Islamic holidays marked tentative may shift by a day depending on moon sighting.

2026.name: New Year's Day
2026.desc: The first day of the Gregorian calendar year, celebrated across India.

2026.name: Lohri
2026.desc: Punjabi winter folk festival with bonfires, celebrating the end of peak winter and the sugarcane harvest.

2026.name: Makar Sankranti
2026.desc: Harvest festival marking the sun's entry into Makara (Capricorn) — famous for kite flying and til-gud sweets.

2026.name: Pongal
2026.desc: Tamil four-day harvest thanksgiving; the first day boils new rice with milk in a decorated pot.

2026.name: Vasant Panchami
2026.desc: Marks the start of spring; devotees honour Goddess Saraswati and wear yellow.

2026.name: Republic Day
2026.desc: India's Constitution came into force on this day in 1950, celebrated with a grand parade in New Delhi.

2026.name: Maha Shivaratri
2026.desc: The great night of Shiva — devotees fast, chant and keep vigil through the night at temples.

2026.name: Shivaji Jayanti
2026.desc: Birth anniversary of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, founder of the Maratha Empire.

2026.name: Holika Dahan
2026.desc: Eve of Holi — bonfires are lit at night to symbolise the burning of the demoness Holika and the victory of good.

2026.name: Holi
2026.desc: The festival of colours — people splash gulal and water, celebrate spring and the victory of good over evil.

2026.name: Ugadi
2026.desc: Telugu and Kannada New Year; homes are decorated with mango leaves and bevu-bella (neem-jaggery) is shared.

2026.name: Gudi Padwa
2026.desc: Maharashtrian New Year — a bright gudi (silk flag with a copper pot) is raised at the doorstep.

2026.name: Eid al-Fitr (Ramzan Id)
2026.desc: End of Ramadan — celebrated with special morning prayers, feasting and giving of zakat al-fitr. Date subject to moon sighting.

2026.name: Rama Navami
2026.desc: Celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, with temple processions and readings of the Ramayana.

2026.name: Mahavir Jayanti
2026.desc: Birth anniversary of Lord Mahavira, the 24th Jain Tirthankara, marked by peaceful processions.

2026.name: Good Friday
2026.desc: Christian commemoration of the crucifixion of Jesus Christ, observed with church services.

2026.name: Easter Sunday
2026.desc: Christian festival of the resurrection of Jesus Christ, celebrated with sunrise services and feasting.

2026.name: Vaisakhi
2026.desc: Punjabi harvest new year and the founding of the Khalsa order in 1699, celebrated with bhangra and nagar kirtans.

2026.name: Ambedkar Jayanti
2026.desc: Birth anniversary of Dr B. R. Ambedkar, principal architect of the Indian Constitution.

2026.name: Bohag Bihu
2026.desc: Assamese spring new year and harvest festival of song, dance and feasting.

2026.name: Buddha Purnima
2026.desc: Commemorates the birth, enlightenment and passing of Gautama Buddha — the most sacred Buddhist festival.

2026.name: Labour Day
2026.desc: Honours workers and the labour movement; observed as May Day in many states.

2026.name: Muharram (Ashura)
2026.desc: Islamic new year period of mourning, especially observed by Shia Muslims with tazia processions.

2026.name: Rath Yatra
2026.desc: Lord Jagannath's grand chariot festival in Puri — colossal wooden raths are pulled through the streets by devotees.

2026.name: Guru Purnima
2026.desc: Day of gurus — students honour their teachers, and Vyasa's birthday is celebrated.

2026.name: Independence Day
2026.desc: India's independence from British rule in 1947, marked by the Prime Minister's Red Fort address.

2026.name: Milad un-Nabi
2026.desc: Birth anniversary of the Prophet Muhammad, observed with prayers and sermons. Date subject to moon sighting.

2026.name: Onam
2026.desc: Kerala's harvest festival welcoming the legendary King Mahabali — pookalam flowers, sadya feast and boat races.

2026.name: Raksha Bandhan
2026.desc: Sisters tie a rakhi thread on their brothers' wrists, symbolising protection and affection.

2026.name: Janmashtami
2026.desc: Birthday of Lord Krishna — midnight celebrations and the famous dahi-handi human pyramids.

2026.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
2026.desc: Ten-day festival welcoming Lord Ganesha, ending with grand visarjan (immersion) processions.

2026.name: Gandhi Jayanti
2026.desc: Birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation — prayers and tributes at Raj Ghat.

2026.name: Sharad Navratri begins
2026.desc: Nine nights of worship of Goddess Durga in her many forms; garba and dandiya nights light up the west.

2026.name: Durga Ashtami
2026.desc: The most important day of Durga Puja — Goddess Durga's fiercest form is worshipped with sandhi puja.

2026.name: Dussehra (Vijayadashami)
2026.desc: Celebrates Rama's victory over Ravana — giant effigies of Ravana are burnt at Ramlila grounds.

2026.name: Karwa Chauth
2026.desc: Married women fast from sunrise to moonrise, praying for their husbands' long life and wellbeing.

2026.name: Diwali (Deepavali)
2026.desc: The festival of lights — diyas, rangoli and fireworks celebrate Rama's return to Ayodhya and Lakshmi puja.

2026.name: Govardhan Puja
2026.desc: Krishna's lifting of Govardhan hill is commemorated; Annakut food mountains are offered in temples.

2026.name: Bhai Dooj
2026.desc: Sisters apply a tilak on their brothers' foreheads and pray for their long life, closing the Diwali season.

2026.name: Chhath Puja
2026.desc: Sun-worship festival of Bihar and UP — devotees fast and offer arghya to the setting and rising sun at riverbanks.

2026.name: Guru Nanak Jayanti
2026.desc: Birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, founder of Sikhism — akhand paths and langar feasts are held.

2026.name: Christmas
2026.desc: Celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ, with midnight mass, carols and festive decorations.
